# 4.6 - Linear Models in the Real World {.unnumbered}

**Main Focus**

* Model real situations with linear equations (motion, cost, temperature, etc.).
* Interpret slope and intercept in context (rate and starting value).
* Sketch or estimate **best-fit lines** informally to describe data trends.

> *Goal:* Use linear equations as modeling tools.

**Teacher Tips / Key Side Points**

* Provide messy or semi-realistic data — they don’t have to be perfect lines.
* Ask: “What does it mean if the slope is bigger?” or “What would a negative slope mean here?”
* Bring in technology (Desmos, spreadsheet trendlines) to visualize best-fit.
* Use units every time (“$5 per hour,” “2 inches per day”) to anchor meaning.
* Briefly mention domain restrictions—what x-values make sense in context.
